## North_Pacific Subtropical Front (STF) and Transition Zone Chlorophyll Front (TZCF)

```{r}
#| include: false
### Load libraries
library(raster)
library(rasterVis)
library(mapdata)
library(cmocean)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(latticeExtra)
library(rerddap)
library(here)
library(sf)
library(nmfspalette)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# Set report year (RptYr), to make things easier
RptYr <- 2024

# Set path to variable: Fisheries Indicators
# This is where the data are and where the plots will go
Dir <- here('Fronts')
```

```{r}
#| include: false

# Set variables that are used by both STF and TZCF figures
# Area for which to make the maps
lat1 <- 45
lat2 <- 5
lon1 <- 180
lon2 <- 240

# Get land information and make it into a spatial object for plotting
land <- maps::map('world2', fill=TRUE, xlim=c(180,240), ylim=c(20,45), plot=FALSE)
landSpat <- as_Spatial(st_as_sf(land))

# Make map themes
mapThemeSST <- rasterTheme(region=rev(brewer.pal(11, 'Spectral')))
mapThemeChl <- rasterTheme(region=cmocean('algae')(50))
mapThemeChl <- rasterTheme(region=nmfs_palette('seagrass')(50))
mapThemeSST <- rasterTheme(region=rev(nmfs_palette('waves')(50)))


```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| include: false

#----------------------------------------------------------
#   STF  
#----------------------------------------------------------
## Download data from erddap
# For temp we are using the Coral Reef Watch product https://oceanwatch.pifsc.noaa.gov/erddap/griddap/CRW_sst_v3_1_monthly.html
# for ease I'm downloading one month at a time for all years, so first Jan then Feb and then March
sstInfo <- info(url = 'https://oceanwatch.pifsc.noaa.gov/erddap', datasetid = 'CRW_sst_v3_1_monthly')
monthIdx <- c(31,28,31)
# Comment below out if you have already downloaded and saved the .nc file
# Looping through to grab files for Jan, then Feb, then March
for (i in 1:3) {
  sstDat <- griddap(sstInfo, time = c(paste0('1985-0',i, '-', monthIdx[i],'T12:00:00Z'), paste0(RptYr, '-0',i,'-', monthIdx[i],'T12:00:00Z')), latitude = c(lat1, lat2), longitude = c(lon1, lon2),
                    fields = sstInfo$variables$variable_name[1],
                    stride = c(12,1,1),
                    store=disk(paste0(Dir,'/STFdata')))
}

```

```{r}
#| include: false

# Read in the files
STFfiles <- list.files(paste0(Dir,'/STFdata'), full.names = T)
# Read all three files into R and combine as stack and sort them after the date (name)
t1 <- brick(STFfiles[1])
t2 <- brick(STFfiles[2])
t3 <- brick(STFfiles[3])

# Make a climatology for 1985-2009
# list years and grab index you need
yr <- substr(names(t1), 2, 5)
climIdx <- which(yr == 2009)
# Average average all the first quarter months for the climatology
tclim <- mean(stack(t1[[1:climIdx]], t2[[1:climIdx]], t3[[1:climIdx]]))

## Make the plot
# Isolate the Report Year for background SST and emphasized contourline and make a dataset
RptIdx <- which(yr==RptYr)
datRptYr <- mean(brick(t1[[RptIdx]],t2[[RptIdx]],t3[[RptIdx]]))
# Start your plot by making the report year background SST with a land overlay
p0 <- levelplot(datRptYr, pretty=T, margin=F, par.setting=mapThemeSST, at=seq(4,29.5,by=0.3), colorkey=list(title=list(label='Sea Surface Temperature (°C)', cex=1), title.control=list(side='right'))) +
        layer(sp.polygons(landSpat, fill='gray50', col='gray30', lwd=0.75))

# Loop through all years of the dataset to add gray ghost contours for each year
# Add each contour to the plot initiated above
for (i in 1:nlayers(t1)) {
  # Average Jan-Mar data for year i
  dat <- mean(brick(t1[[i]],t2[[i]],t3[[i]]))
  # Make ith year contour
  p1 <- contourplot(dat, pretty=T, margin=F, cuts=1, at=18, labels=F, lwd=0.5, par.settings = list(add.line = list(col = "lightgray")))
  # Add contour to plot
  p0 <- p0+p1
}
# Finally add the climatology contour as a dashed line and the report year contour as a solid black line
p0 <- p0 + 
        contourplot(datRptYr, pretty=T, margin=F, cuts=1, at=18, labels=F) + 
        contourplot(tclim, pretty=T, margin=F, cuts=1, at=18, labels=F, lty=2)
        

# Save plot
png(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_STFmap_', RptYr, '.png'), width=7, height=5, res=300, units='in') 
p0
dev.off()

```

```{r}
#| echo: false

# Figure caption text
# Average position of the subtropical front (STF) in 2023 (solid black line), over the 1985–2009 average (dotted line), locations from previous years (1985–2024; solid grey lines), and ocean temperatures for the first quarter of 2024 (shaded). 

knitr::include_graphics(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_STFmap_', RptYr, '.png'))

```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| include: false

#----------------------------------------------------------
#   TCZF
#----------------------------------------------------------

## Download data from erddap
# for ease I'm downloading one month at a time for all years, so first Jan then Feb and then March
chlInfo <- info(url = 'https://oceanwatch.pifsc.noaa.gov/erddap', datasetid = 'esa-cci-chla-monthly-v6-0')
# Comment below out if you have already downloaded and saved the .nc file
# Looping through to grab files for Jan, then Feb, then March
for (i in 1:3) {
  chlDat <- griddap(chlInfo, time = c(paste0('1998-0',i, '-01'),paste0(RptYr, '-0',i, '-01')), latitude = c(lat2, lat1), longitude = c(lon1, lon2),
                    fields = chlInfo$variables$variable_name[1],
                    stride = c(12,1,1),
                    store=disk(paste0(Dir,'/TZCFdata')))
}

```

```{r}
#| include: false

# Read in the files
TZCFfiles <- list.files(paste0(Dir,'/TZCFdata/'), full.names = T)
# Read all three files into R and combine as stack and sort them after the date (name)
c1 <- brick(TZCFfiles[1])
c2 <- brick(TZCFfiles[2])
c3 <- brick(TZCFfiles[3])
# Make a climatology for 1998-2009
# list years and grab index you need
yr <- substr(names(c1), 2, 5)
climIdx <- which(yr == 2009)
# Average average all the first quarter months for the climatology
cclim <- mean(stack(c1[[1:climIdx]], c2[[1:climIdx]], c3[[1:climIdx]]), na.rm=T)
# aggregate the raster to 0.5 degree for nicer plotting. Take the mean of aggregated cells
cclim <- aggregate(cclim, fact=12, fun=mean)
cclim_crop <- crop(cclim, extent(c(180, 240.5, 29, 40))) # to clean up the areas around the front and make figure less busy

## Make the plot
# Isolate the Report Year for background SST and emphasized contourline and make a dataset
RptIdx <- which(yr==RptYr)
datRptYrC <- aggregate(mean(brick(c1[[RptIdx]],c2[[RptIdx]],c3[[RptIdx]])), fact=3, fun=mean)
datRptYrC5 <- aggregate(mean(brick(c1[[RptIdx]],c2[[RptIdx]],c3[[RptIdx]])), fact=12, fun=mean)

# Start your plot by making the report year background SST with a land overlay
pC0 <- levelplot(datRptYrC, pretty=T, margin=F, par.setting=mapThemeChl, at=seq(0,0.8,by=0.01),
                 colorkey=list(title=list(label=expression(Chlorophyll-a ~ Concentration ~ (mg/m^3)), cex=1), 
                               title.control=list(side='right'))) 

# Loop through all years of the dataset to add gray ghost contours for each year
# Add each contour to the plot initiated above
for (i in 1:nlayers(c1)) {
  # Average Jan-Mar data for year i
  datC <- crop(aggregate(mean(brick(c1[[i]],c2[[i]],c3[[i]])), fact=12, fun=mean), extent(c(180, 240.5, 27, 42)))
  # Make ith year contour
  pC1 <- contourplot(datC, pretty=T, margin=F, at=0.2, labels=F, par.settings = list(add.line = list(col = "gray60")))
  # Add contour to plot
  pC0 <- pC0+pC1
}
# Finally add the climatology contour as a dashed line and the report year contour as a solid black line
pC0 <- pC0 + 
        contourplot(crop(datRptYrC5, extent(c(180, 240.5, 25, 40))), pretty=T, margin=F, at=0.2, labels=F, lwd=1.25) +
        contourplot(cclim_crop, pretty=T, margin=F, at=0.2, labels=F, lty=2, lwd=1.25) +
        layer(sp.polygons(landSpat, fill='gray50', col='gray30', lwd=0.75))

# Save plot
png(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_TZCFmap_', RptYr, '.png'), width=7, height=5, res=300, units='in') 
pC0
dev.off()

# png(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_TZCFmap_', RptYr, '_only25All.png'), width=7, height=5, res=300, units='in')

#   contourplot(crop(datRptYrC,extent(c(180, 240.5, 29, 40))), pretty=T, margin=F, at=0.2, labels=F, lwd=1.25) +
#   contourplot(cclim_crop, pretty=T, margin=F, at=0.2, labels=F, lty=2, lwd=1.25) +
#   layer(sp.polygons(landSpat, fill='gray40', col='gray30'))
# dev.off()

```

```{r}
#| echo: false

# Figure caption text
# Average position of the transition zone chlorophyll front (TZCF) in 2023 (solid black line) over the 1998–2009 average (dotted black line) and ocean color for the first quarter of 2023 (shaded).  

knitr::include_graphics(paste0(Dir, '/SAFE_TZCFmap_', RptYr, '.png'))

```

Rationale: The STF is targeted by the swordfish fishery. Additionally, both the STF and TZCF are used as migration and foraging corridors by both commercially valuable and protected species. Northward displacement of the frontal zone can increase the distance fishing vessels must travel to set their gear. This can, in turn, increase operational expenses. The positions of the fronts vary in response to natural climate variations. Long-term northward displacement of the frontal zone may also result from anthropogenic climate change.\
\
Status: During the first quarter of `r RptYr`, the STF was north of average across much of the fishing grounds. Though, unlike 2022, it was not near its historical northern limits. The TZCF was average across much of the fishing grounds, except between about 170°W and 155°W, where it was slightly north of average.\
\
Description: The subtropical front (STF) is marked by the 18 °C sea surface temperature (SST) isotherm and the transition zone chlorophyll front (TZCF) by the 0.2 mg/m^3^ chl-a isopleth (Bograd et al. 2004; Polovina et al. 2001). They roughly mark the northern boundary of the North Pacific subtropical gyre as well as the northern extent of the Hawaiʻi-based longline fishery. Both fronts migrate meridionally on a seasonal basis and their positions are impacted by the phase of the El Niño – Southern Oscillation (ENSO). Due to significant seasonal variation, the climatology and anomaly (`r RptYr`) are presented for the first quarter of the year only. The STF is determined from CoralTemp data (see SST indicator) and the TZCF is determined from ESA CCI data (see Section 0).\
\
Timeframe: Annual, seasonal\
\
Region: Hawaiʻi longline region: 5° – 45°N, 180° – 120°W\
\
Measurement Platform: Satellite\
\
Data available at: https://oceanwatch.pifsc.noaa.gov/erddap/griddap/CRW_sst_v3_1_monthly and https://oceanwatch.pifsc.noaa.gov/erddap/griddap/esa-cci-chla-monthly-v5-0.\
\
Sourced from: Bograd et al. (2004), Polovina et al. (2001), and NOAA OceanWatch (2024a; 2024b).\
\
